Risk Factors Summary
paragraphs: Eton is an innovative pharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing treatments for rare diseases. We currently have eight commercial rare disease products: INCRELEX®, ALKINDI SPRINKLE®, KHINDIVITM, GALZIN®, PKU GOLIKE®, Carglumic Acid, Betaine Anhydrous, and Nitisinone. We have five additional product candidates in late-stage development: ET-600, Amglidia®, ET-700, ET-800 and ZENEO® hydrocortisone autoinjector.

INCRELEX® – This biologic product was approved by the FDA in August 2005 as a treatment for children who suffer from severe primary insulin-like growth factor 1 deficiency (SPIGFD). The product is approved in 40 territories, including the United States and the European Union. We acquired and launched the product in December 2024.

ALKINDI SPRINKLE® – This product was approved by the FDA in September 2020 as a replacement therapy for Adrenocortical Insufficiency ("AI") in children under 17 years of age. The product is the first and only FDA-approved granule hydrocortisone formulation designed to help provide accurate dosing for newborns and children with AI. We acquired U.S. marketing rights to the product in March 2020 and launched ALKINDI SPRINKLE® in December 2020 with a sales force targeting pediatric endocrinologists. We believe there are approximately 10,000 children currently suffering from AI in the United States. ALKINDI SPRINKLE® is protected by three issued patents that extend to 2032, 2033, and 2034.

KHINDIVITM – This product was approved by the FDA in May 2025 as a replacement therapy in pediatric patients five years of age and older for adrenocortical insufficiency. KHINDIVI is the only FDA-approved oral solution formulation of hydrocortisone. It comes in a 1mg/ml strength designed to eliminate the need to split or crush tablets, and to offer simple and accurate dosing specifically tailored to each patient's needs. It does not require refrigeration, mixing, or shaking – it is a ready-to-use oral liquid solution. KHINDIVI is designed to offer administration simplicity and dosing accuracy, and to provide a therapy option for patients who have difficulty swallowing tablets or with special administration needs, such as patients with a gastric tube.

GALZIN® is FDA-approved as a maintenance treatment for patients with Wilson disease who have been initially treated with a chelating agent. It is estimated that less than 5,000 patients in the U.S. are currently being treated for Wilson disease. We acquired the product in December 2024 and assumed the commercialization of the product in the U.S. in March 2025. We offer the product through our Eton Cares patient support program that provides high-touch, personalized service tailored for rare disease patients and their providers.

PKU GOLIKE® - In March 2024, we acquired the U.S. rights to PKU GOLIKE, which is a next generation medical formula product engineered with the patent protected, pharmaceutical grade Physiomimic™ technology for the dietary management of phenylketonuria ("PKU") under medical supervision. PKU GOLIKE's® taste-masked, odor-free coating technology is designed to provide a better taste and a superior experience compared to alternative PKU medical formulas. In addition, PKU GOLIKE's delayed amino acid release formulation is designed to keep patients full for a longer period of time.

Carglumic Acid Tablets – Our Carglumic Acid product is an FDA-approved generic version of Carbaglu®. Our product is approved for the treatment of acute and chronic hyperammonemia due to N-acetylglutamate synthase ("NAGS") deficiency. We acquired the marketing rights to the product in October 2021 and launched the product in December 2021. We promote the product with our internal sales force.

Betaine Anhydrous for Oral Solution – Our Betaine Anhydrous product is an FDA-approved generic version of Cystadane® for the treatment of homocystinuria, a rare inherited condition that is estimated to impact fewer than 2,000 patients in the United States. We acquired the product in September 2022 and launched the product in May 2023.

Nitisinone – Our Nitisinone product is an FDA-approved generic version of Orfadin® for the treatment of tyrosinemia type 1, an ultra-rare inherited condition that is estimated to impact fewer than 500 patients in the United States. We acquired the product in October 2023 and launched the product in February 2024.

ET-600 – In July 2025, ET-600's NDA was accepted for review by the FDA and assigned a PDUFA target action date of February 25, 2026. The Company has scheduled the production of launch inventory for the first quarter of 2026 in preparation for a commercial launch shortly after the anticipated approval. The Company recently held an ET-600 advisory meeting with leading healthcare practitioners within the pediatric endocrinology community.

Amglidia® - In November 2024, we entered into a licensing agreement with AMMTeK., pursuant to which we have agreed to acquire the U.S. rights to Amglidia® (glyburide oral suspension), which we also have a license to the issued patent on Amglidia®. Amglidia® is being developed for the treatment of neonatal diabetes mellitus, a rare condition estimated to impact approximately 300 patients in the U.S. The product was approved by the European Medicines Agency in 2018 and has been granted Orphan Drug Designation by the FDA. AMMTeK has conducted a post-approval study tracking five years of real-world safety and efficacy in European patients, which will be used to support Eton's NDA submission.

ET-700– We are scheduled to begin its proof-of-concept positron emission tomography ("PET") study during 2026. The study is expected to validate the efficacy of the Company's propriety, patent-pending extended-release formulation, and if positive, would support the initiation of a dose ranging and pivotal clinical trial in late 2026 or early 2027. We have also submitted a patent for ET-700, which is currently pending.

headings: Risks Relating to Pricing, Reimbursement and Market Access
The Inflation Reduction Act and related Medicare reforms may adversely affect the prices we realize and the demand for our products.

Our participation in U.S. government price reporting and discount programs imposes complex and evolving obligations that could adversely affect the net prices we realize and expose us to significant liabilities.
Third-party coverage and reimbursement and healthcare cost containment initiatives, including formulary controls and utilization management, may constrain our future revenues.
Risks Relating to Our Business
We may need to grow the size of our organization, and we could experience difficulties in managing this growth.
We focus on rare diseases, which may create additional risks and challenges, including that the target patient populations of our products and product candidates may be small.
If product liability lawsuits are brought against us, we may incur substantial liabilities and may be required to limit commercialization of our product candidates.
We may acquire businesses or products, or form strategic alliances, in the future, and we may not realize the benefits of such acquisitions.
Risks Related to Product Development, Regulatory Approval, Manufacturing and Commercialization
We face competition from other biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies and our operating results will suffer if we fail to compete effectively.
We face substantial competition, which may result in others discovering, developing and commercializing products before or more successfully than our product candidates.

If we are not able to obtain any required regulatory approvals for our product candidates, we will not be able to commercialize our product candidate and our ability to generate revenue will be limited.
An NDA submitted under Section 505(b)(2) subjects us to the risk that we may be subject to a patent infringement lawsuit that would delay or prevent the review or approval of our product candidate.

Even if we receive regulatory approval for our additional product candidates, we may not be able to successfully commercialize these products, and the revenue that we generate from those sales, if any, may be limited.
We are subject to Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements, and failure to comply could disrupt our distribution and result in enforcement action.
Significant additional labeling or warning requirements or limitations on the availability of our products may inhibit sales of affected products.
paragraphs: We operate in a dynamic and rapidly changing environment that involves numerous risks and uncertainties. Certain factors may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations, and you should carefully consider them. Accordingly, in evaluating our business, we encourage you to consider the following discussion of risk factors, in its entirety, in addition to other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and our other public filings with the SEC. Other events that we do not currently anticipate or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our results of operations and financial condition.

The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (the "IRA"), and related federal and state healthcare reforms, have introduced new and evolving mechanisms that may affect the prices we realize for our products and the demand for our products over time. These mechanisms include, among others, inflation-based rebates under Medicare Parts B and D that can require payments when certain reported prices increase faster than inflation; changes to the Medicare Part D benefit beginning in 2025 that redistribute financial liability among manufacturers, plans and the government while capping patient out-of-pocket costs; and a program under which certain drugs may become subject to price negotiation on a defined timetable. The applicability and impact of these mechanisms will evolve over time based on our portfolio mix and the characteristics of individual products. For example, whether and when a product becomes subject to the Medicare drug price negotiation program depends, among other factors, on the time elapsed since FDA approval and other selection criteria, and inflation‑based rebates in Medicare Parts B and D apply when prices increase faster than inflation. Changes in our portfolio, utilization and payer mix could therefore alter our exposure to negotiation, inflation‑based rebates, and the redesigned Medicare Part D benefit, including our financial responsibility under the new benefit structure. Implementation will occur through ongoing regulatory actions, the outcomes of which remain uncertain. Even where our current products are not immediately selected for negotiation or have limited Medicare utilization, these changes may alter channel economics, increase our obligations, reduce the net prices we realize, and adversely affect patient access and demand. Certain statutory exemptions may apply to particular products based on their indications, approval history or other factors; however, exemptions are narrow and can change with future legislation, guidance or changes in our product portfolio. The IRA, its implementing regulations and related guidance continue to evolve, and the scope and timing of their impact on our business remains uncertain.

Our participation in U.S. government price reporting and discount programs materially affects the net prices we realize and requires us to comply with complex and evolving legal and reporting obligations. For example, under the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, we must calculate and report Average Manufacturer Price ("AMP") and, where applicable, Best Price, and pay rebates to states. Recalculations or restatements—whether due to errors, new interpretations, government audits or other factors—can be retroactive and may require us to pay additional rebates. These obligations can also affect pricing and refund requirements under the 340B Drug Pricing Program, including through recalculation of ceiling prices and controls intended to prevent duplicate discounts. In addition, our products may be subject to pricing and discount requirements under the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and Federal Supply Schedule programs, including obligations tied to Non-Federal Average Manufacturer Price ("Non-FAMP"), Federal Ceiling Price ("FCP") and related certifications, as well as TRICARE rebate requirements. Government authorities continue to increase scrutiny of these programs, and noncompliance (including inaccurate reporting, failure to timely report changes, or failure to implement required controls) may result in significant refunds, civil monetary penalties, contractual damages, suspension or termination from participation in government programs, reputational harm, and potential liability under the False Claims Act.

Our ability to successfully commercialize our products and product candidates depends in significant part on the extent to which governmental authorities, commercial insurers and other third-party payors provide coverage for, and establish adequate reimbursement levels for, our products. Even if a product is approved, payors may limit or exclude coverage, place the product at a disadvantageous formulary tier, require prior authorization, impose step-therapy or other utilization management restrictions, or require patients to pay higher out-of-pocket costs. Pharmacy benefit managers ("PBMs") and payors may also increase their leverage through formulary exclusions, restrictive network arrangements, and demands for greater rebates, discounts or other price concessions, which can increase our gross-to-net reductions and reduce realized prices. In addition, treatment guidelines, clinical pathways, and health technology assessment frameworks may influence prescribing behavior and coverage determinations. If coverage and reimbursement are inadequate, delayed or more restrictive than we anticipate, or if our gross-to-net reductions increase, our sales, profitability and results of operations could be adversely affected.

We may operate or support patient services and assistance programs, and government scrutiny of these activities could require us to curtail such programs, reducing patient access and adversely affecting demand for our products.

We may operate or support patient services, including product access hubs, patient assistance programs, or programs that help patients address out-of-pocket costs. Government authorities have increased scrutiny of these activities, including our interactions with third-party service providers and independent charitable foundations, and the application of fraud and abuse laws to certain patient support arrangements. Evolving guidance, audits, investigations or enforcement actions could require us to modify, curtail or discontinue some of these programs or arrangements. If patient services or assistance programs are reduced or not available on terms that support patient access, patients may be unable to afford our products, prescription abandonment may increase, and demand and net sales could decline. Investigations or enforcement actions could also result in significant costs, penalties, settlements, or reputational harm.

paragraphs: Eton 是一家創新製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化罕見疾病的治療方案。目前本公司有八種已上市的罕見疾病產品：INCRELEX®、ALKINDI SPRINKLE®、KHINDIVITM、GALZIN®、PKU GOLIKE®、Carglumic Acid、Betaine Anhydrous 以及 Nitisinone。本公司尚有五種產品候選藥物處於後期開發階段：ET-600、Amglidia®、ET-700、ET-800 以及 ZENEO® hydrocortisone 自動注射器。
INCRELEX® – 此生物製劑產品於 2005 年 8 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，用於治療罹患嚴重原發性胰島素樣生長因子 1 缺乏症（SPIGFD）的兒童。此產品已獲批准於 40 個管轄區域，包括美國與歐盟。本公司於 2024 年 12 月取得並上市此產品。

ALKINDI SPRINKLE® – 此產品於 2020 年 9 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，作為 17 歲以下兒童罹患腎上腺皮質功能不足（"AI"）的替代治療方案。此產品為美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的首個且唯一之顆粒型氫化可的松製劑，設計用以協助提供準確劑量給新生兒與 AI 罹患兒童。本公司於 2020 年 3 月取得美國市場權，並於 2020 年 12 月上市 ALKINDI SPRINKLE®，搭配專門針對小兒內分泌科醫生的銷售團隊。本公司認為美國約有 10,000 名兒童罹患 AI。ALKINDI SPRINKLE® 由三項已發明專利保護，專利期限分別至 2032 年、2033 年與 2034 年。

KHINDIVITM – 此產品於 2025 年 5 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，作為五歲以上兒童罹患腎上腺皮質功能不足的替代治療方案。KHINDIVI 是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的唯一口服液態氫化可的松製劑。其 1mg/ml 強度設計可消除需分割或壓碎片劑的需要，並提供簡單且準確的劑量，針對每位患者的需要進行調整。此產品無需冷藏、混合或搖晃，為即開即用的口服液體製劑。KHINDIVI 設計用以提供簡易的給藥方式與準確的劑量，並為有吞嚥片劑困難或特殊給藥需求的患者（如胃管患者）提供治療選擇。
GALZIN® 美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准作為 Wilson 病患者初始治療使用螯合劑後的維持治療。估計美國目前接受 Wilson 病治療的患者少於 5,000 名。本公司於 2024 年 12 月取得此產品，並於 2025 年 3 月開始於美國進行商業化。本公司透過 Eton Cares 患者支持計畫提供此產品，該計畫提供高接觸、個性化服務，專為罕見疾病患者及其醫療提供者設計。

PKU GOLIKE® – 本公司於 2024 年 3 月取得 PKU GOLIKE 的美國權利，此產品為新一代醫療配方產品，採用專利保護的藥物等級 Physiomimic™ 技術，用於在醫療監督下管理苯酮尿症（"PKU"）。PKU GOLIKE® 的味道掩蔽、無氣味包裝技術設計用以提供較佳的口感與優越的使用體驗，與其他 PKU 醫療配方相比。此外，PKU GOLIKE® 的延遲氨基酸釋放配方設計用以讓患者較長時間保持飽足感。
Carglumic Acid 片劑 – 本公司 Carglumic Acid 產品為 FDA 批准的 Carbaglu® 通用藥品。此產品批准用於治療因 N-乙醯谷氨醯胺合成酶（"NAGS"）缺乏引起的急性與慢性高氨血癥。本公司於 2021 年 10 月取得此產品的市場權，並於 2021 年 12 月上市此產品。本公司透過內部銷售團隊推廣此產品。
Betaine Anhydrous 口服液體 – 本公司 Betaine Anhydrous 產品為 FDA 批准的 Cystadane® 通用藥品，用於治療罕見遺傳性疾病同型半胱胺酸尿症，估計美國受此疾病影響的患者少於 2,000 名。本公司於 2022 年 9 月取得此產品，並於 2023 年 5 月上市此產品。
Nitisinone – 本公司之 Nitisinone 產品為美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准之 Orfadin® 仿製藥，用以治療酪胺酸血癥第一型，為一種極為罕見的遺傳性疾病，估計在美國影響少於 500 名患者。本公司於 2023 年 10 月取得該產品，並於 2024 年 2 月推出該產品。
ET-600 – 2025 年 7 月，ET-600 之新藥申請（NDA）已獲 FDA 接受審查，並指定 2026 年 2 月 25 日為 PDUFA 預期行動日期。本公司已安排於 2026 年第一季進行上市存貨之生產，以準備於預期核准後不久進行商業上市。本公司最近與小兒內分泌學領域之領先醫療專業人員舉行了 ET-600 專案諮詢會議。

Amglidia® - 2024 年 11 月，本公司與 AMMTeK 簽訂授權協議，根據協議，本公司同意取得 Amglidia®（glyburide 口服懸浮液）之美國權利，本公司亦擁有 Amglidia® 發行專利之授權。Amglidia® 正在開發用以治療新生兒糖尿病，為一種罕見疾病，估計在美國影響約 300 名患者。該產品於 2018 年獲歐洲藥物管理局核准，並已獲得 FDA 獨家藥物指定（Orphan Drug Designation）。AMMTeK 已進行一項上市後研究，追蹤歐洲患者五年的實際安全與療效，將用以支持 Eton 之 NDA 申請。
ET-700 – 本公司預計於 2026 年開始進行其概念驗證正子發射斷層掃描（"PET"）研究。該研究預期將驗證本公司之專利中藥物延效製劑之療效，若結果為正，將支持於 2026 年底或 2027 年初啟動劑量範圍與關鍵臨牀試驗。本公司亦已提交 ET-700 之專利申請，目前尚在審查中。

headings: 與定價、報銷及市場准入相關的風險
《降低通貨膨脹法案》及相關的醫療保險改革措施可能不利於我們所實現的價格及對我們產品的需求。
本公司參與美國政府價格報告及折扣計畫，會產生複雜且不斷演變的義務，這可能會不利於我們所實現的淨價格，並使我們面臨重大賠償責任。
第三方保險範圍及報銷及醫療費用控制措施，包括處方藥清單管理及使用管理，可能限制我們未來的收入。
與本公司業務相關的風險
我們可能需要擴大組織規模，我們可能會面臨管理此擴張的困難。
我們專注於罕見疾病，這可能會產生額外的風險與挑戰，包括我們產品及產品候選藥物的目標患者羣可能規模較小。
如果有人對我們提出產品責任訴訟，我們可能會面臨重大賠償責任，並可能被要求限制我們產品候選藥物的商業化。
本公司未來可能取得企業或產品，或成立策略聯盟，但未必能實現這些取得行動的效益。
與產品開發、法規核准、製造與商業化相關的風險
本公司面臨來自其他生物科技與製藥公司的競爭，若本公司無法有效競爭，營運成果將受到影響。
本公司面臨相當程度的競爭，這可能會導致其他公司先於本公司或更成功地發現、開發並商業化產品。
若本公司無法取得任何所需法規核准，將無法商業化產品候選品，且本公司產生收入的能力將受到限制。
根據第 505(b)(2) 節提交的新藥申請（NDA），本公司可能面臨專利侵權訴訟的風險，這可能會延宕或阻止產品候選品的審查或核准。
即使本公司取得額外產品候選品的法規核准，本公司可能仍無法成功商業化這些產品，且若有任何銷售收入，其金額可能受到限制。
本公司須遵守藥物供應鏈安全法案（Drug Supply Chain Security Act）的規定，若未能遵守，可能幹擾本公司之分銷，並導致執法行動。

paragraphs: 我們營運於一個動態且快速變化的環境中，涉及許多風險與不確定性。某些因素可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響，您應仔細考量這些因素。因此，在評估我們的業務時，我們鼓勵您一併考量以下風險因素的完整討論，以及本年度報告表10-K及我們其他公開提交至SEC的資料。其他我們目前未預期或認為不重要的事件，也可能影響我們的營運成果與財務狀況。

2022年《通貨膨脹減免法案》（"IRA"），以及相關的聯邦與州級醫療改革，已引入新的且持續演進的機制，可能影響我們產品的售價與產品需求。這些機制包括，例如，根據醫療保險B與D部分的通貨膨脹補償，當報告價格增長快於通貨膨脹時，可能要求支付補償；2025年起醫療保險D部分福利的變更，重新分配製造商、計畫與政府之間的財務責任，同時限制患者自付費用；以及某些藥物可能根據既定時間表進行價格談判的計畫。這些機制的適用性與影響將根據我們的產品組合與個別產品的特性而持續演進。例如，產品是否及何時會成為醫療保險藥物價格談判計畫的對象，取決於多種因素，包括自FDA核准以來的時間及其他選拔標準，而醫療保險B與D部分的通貨膨脹補償則適用於價格增長快於通貨膨脹的情況。因此，我們產品組合、使用率與支付者結構的變化，可能改變我們對談判、通貨膨脹補償及重新設計的醫療保險D部分福利的暴露程度，包括我們在新福利結構下的財務責任。這些機制的實施將透過持續的法規行動進行，其結果仍不確定。即使目前產品未立即被選為談判對象或在醫療保險中的使用有限，這些變化仍可能改變通路經濟學、增加我們的義務、降低我們實現的淨售價，並不利於患者取得與需求。

我們參與美國政府的價格報告與折扣計畫，會對我們實現的淨售價產生重大影響，並要求我們遵守複雜且持續演進的法律與報告義務。例如，根據醫療保險藥物補償計畫，我們必須計算並報告平均製造商價格（"AMP"），並在適用時報告最佳價格，並向各州支付補償。重新計算或修正—無論是因錯誤、新解釋、政府稽核或其他因素—可能具有追溯效力，並可能要求我們支付額外補償。這些義務也可能影響340B藥物價格計畫下的價格與退款要求，包括透過重新計算天花板價格及防止重複折扣的控制措施。此外，我們的產品可能受美國退伍軍人事務部與聯邦供應計畫下的價格與折扣要求影響，包括與非聯邦平均製造商價格（"Non-FAMP"）、聯邦天花板價格（"FCP"）及相關認證，以及TRICARE補償要求相關的義務。政府機構持續增加對這些計畫的審查，不遵守（包括報告不正確、未及時報告變更或未實施所需控制）可能導致重大退款、民事罰款、契約損害、被終止參與政府計畫、聲譽損害，以及根據虛假申報法的潛在責任。

我們成功商業化產品與產品候選品的能力，在很大程度上取決於政府機構、商業保險公司及其他第三方支付者是否為我們的產品提供覆蓋，並建立足夠的報銷水平。即使產品獲得核准，支付者可能限制或排除覆蓋、將產品放置於不利的處方層級、要求事前授權、施加分階段治療或其他使用管理限制，或要求患者支付更高的自付費用。藥物福利管理機構（"PBMs"）與支付者也可能透過處方層級排除、限制性網路安排及要求更高的補償、折扣或其他價格讓步，增加我們的毛利率至淨銷售減損，並降低實現的售價。此外，治療指南、臨牀路徑及健康科技評估框架可能影響處方行為與覆蓋決定。如果覆蓋與報銷不足、延遲或比預期更嚴格，或我們的毛利率至淨銷售減損增加，將可能對我們的銷售、利潤及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們可能運營或支援患者服務與協助計畫，而政府對這些活動的審查可能要求我們縮減這些計畫，降低患者取得能力，並對我們產品的需求產生不利影響。

我們可能運營或支援患者服務，包括產品取得中心、患者協助計畫，或協助患者處理自付費用的計畫。政府機構已增加對這些活動的審查，包括我們與第三方服務供應商及獨立慈善基金的互動，以及某些患者支援安排適用詐欺與濫用法規。持續演進的指導方針、稽核、調查或執法行動可能要求我們修改、縮減或終止部分這些計畫或安排。如果患者服務或協助計畫被縮減或無法在支持患者取得的條件下提供，患者可能無法負擔我們的產品，處方放棄率可能增加，導致需求與淨銷售下降。調查或執法行動也可能導致重大成本、罰款、和解或聲譽損害。
